summary: M3.1 turns M2.1's compile-only cooperative_matrix codegen into the FIRST-EVER real tensor-core dispatch and builds the GPU-resident benchmark methodology that M3.0's <1ms gate was re-scoped onto. r1 closes the four blocking CRITICALs from the pessimistic review: (C1) coopmat shape is now real metadata — HIR carries a kernel-level CoopMatShape derived from the body's matrix types, CoopMatKey gains k + result_type, and KernelMetadata gains a serde-default `coopmat` field with a schema bump 1→2 + back-compat, so the runtime builds CoopMatRequiredShape FROM METADATA (HN-10/AT-1551 now real, not a literal); (C2/C3) a binding-plan-driven `required_device_features` pass enables storageBuffer16BitAccess (f16 SSBO) and storageBuffer8BitAccess+shaderInt8+shaderInt16 (q4km u8) — these are the FIRST 8/16-bit kernels ever dispatched and context.rs currently enables NONE of them; missing features fail-closed with the typed DeviceFeatureUnsupported skip; (C4) AT-1510 uses a non-symmetric transpose-distinguishing fixture so a transposed/swapped/mis-strided coopmat_load cannot pass. Deliverables: (A) coopmat dispatch (VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix + cooperativeMatrix + VulkanMemoryModel + 16-bit storage features, preflight, subgroupSize==32 guard, graceful typed skip); (B) plain multi-row q4km matmul bit-exact 256x256 (runs everywhere, NOT #[ignore]) + staged pre-dequantized coopmat bridge (NVIDIA-only); (C) GPU-resident benchmark (upload-once/dispatch-N/kernel-only-timing); (D) per-vendor @strategy tile holes preflight-validated; (E) Lever A readback skip for readonly bindings, re-landed without ReBAR. AT range AT-1500..AT-1561. spirv-val + clippy -D warnings + cargo test --workspace (+ --ignored) green; existing public API and bench IDs preserved.

staged_explicitly_deferred: FULL Q4_K_M-dequant-output FED DIRECTLY into coopmat_load/mul_add as f16 A/B matrices in ONE kernel is the hardest integration: it requires dequantizing into a workgroup-shared f16 tile (shared[T,N] — FG.6, NOT yet a language feature, folded into M3.2) before coopmat_load can read a contiguous row-major f16 tile. Therefore the 256x256 q4km bit-exact deliverable (AT-1520) is produced by the multi-row dequant+matmul kernel WITHOUT coopmat (each output = the M2.6 dequant dot-product, tiled), which is provably bit-exact and dispatchable TODAY. The plain-f16 matmul_tile dispatch is the coopmat PROOF; the multi-row q4km matmul is the REAL-WORKLOAD bit-exact deliverable; the fused coopmat-q4km is the forward-looking bridge to M3.4.

cublas_comparison_method.how_obtained: There is NO cuBLAS dependency in-tree (the project is CUDA-free by thesis). The percent-of-cuBLAS figure is evaluated against a DOCUMENTED external cuBLAS f32 GEMM throughput for the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, recorded as a named constant CUBLAS_F32_GEMM_TFLOPS_RTX_PRO_6000 in crates/axc-driver/tests/common_matmul.rs with a sourced comment (specific datasheet/microbench URL). The bench reports EFFECTIVE TFLOPS = 2*M*N*K / kernel_seconds for the 4096x4096 resident matmul and prints both the measured TFLOPS and the percent-of-cuBLAS ratio.
cublas_comparison_method.honesty: The percent-of-cuBLAS is an ESTIMATE, LABELED 'estimate (external cuBLAS baseline)' in bench output and in DESIGN §3.1.13. It is NOT a same-machine A/B. The UNCONDITIONALLY HONEST number is the in-tree effective TFLOPS, fully reproducible. AT-1532 asserts ONLY that effective TFLOPS is finite and > 0 (the >=50% claim is informational, NOT a hard assertion). The constant is asserted > 0 && finite as a sanity check. Mirrors M3.0's acceptance-honesty discipline.

The runtime computes the required set from `required_device_features(binding_plan, kernel_uses_coopmat)`. FAIL-CLOSED: if a required feature is unavailable on the device, dispatch returns DispatchError::DeviceFeatureUnsupported (or CoopMatUnsupported for coopmat-specific) — never enable-and-hope.

transpose_fixture_spec.shape: 16x16 f16 tiles, row-major, stride 16, C0 = 0 (16x16 zeros).
transpose_fixture_spec.A: A[i][j] = f16(1.0 + 0.5*i - 0.25*j)  for i,j in 0..16  — a row-gradient: rows increase, columns decrease. A is NOT symmetric (A[i][j] != A[j][i]) and NOT constant.
transpose_fixture_spec.B: B[i][j] = f16(-0.5 + 0.5*j + 0.125*i)  for i,j in 0..16  — a column-gradient distinct from A. B is NOT symmetric and B != A and B != A^T.
transpose_fixture_spec.C_expected: C[i][j] = sum_{k=0..16} A[i][k]*B[k][j], accumulated in f32 then rounded to f16 (matmul_tile_16x16x16_f16_cpu).
transpose_fixture_spec.why_transpose_distinguishing: Because A is row-monotone and B is column-monotone with different slopes/offsets, A·B, Aᵀ·B, A·Bᵀ, and B·A produce different value SURFACES: e.g. element (0,0): A·B uses A row0 (small) · B col0 (small) while B·A uses B row0 · A col0 (different magnitudes); element (15,0) and (0,15) diverge strongly between a product and its transpose because the i- and j- gradients are asymmetric. AT-1512 asserts that for the chosen fixtures, max_elementwise_abs_diff(AB, AtB) , (AB, ABt) , (AB, BA) each exceed 10x the per-element f16 tolerance at one or more elements — i.e. a transpose/swap/stride bug is numerically detectable. The Coder must compute the four CPU references and assert the pairwise max diffs exceed the tolerance band before relying on AT-1510.
transpose_fixture_spec.tolerance: per-element tol = max(2 f16 ULP at the element magnitude, 2^-9 * max(|a_row|,|b_col| accumulated)). For these magnitudes (|A|,|B| <= ~8, K=16, |C| <= ~ a few hundred) the f32-accumulate-then-round reference vs the tensor-core result agree to a handful of ULP; the transpose differences are O(100x) larger, so the test is decisive.

On a wave64 device that advertises 16x16x16 f16 Subgroup, RETURN CoopMatUnsupported (do NOT dispatch) — prevents silent miscompute. AMD/Intel remapping is EB.1/M3.4.

Per SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix the accumulation precision is implementation-defined. matmul_tile_16x16x16_f16_cpu accumulates each 16-element dot product in f32 then ROUNDS to f16. The oracle is 'within f16 fp tol' (f16_tile_tol), NOT bit-exact. Do NOT assert raw bit equality of the f16 result tile.

HN-6 (resident timing: validity + masking + reset ordering). Use GPU timestamps only when timestamp_period>0 AND compute timestamp_valid_bits>0. masked_timestamp_delta: mask BOTH begin and end to valid_bits FIRST, then wrapping_sub, then * timestamp_period (mask-before-subtract — WARNING fix; AT-1535 unit-tests the boundary case). cmd_reset_query_pool MUST be recorded BEFORE the first write_timestamp in the SAME submission (or host-side reset) so re-dispatch in the N-loop is well-defined. When unavailable, fall back to CpuFenceWall; record timing_source honestly. Note: TOP_OF_PIPE measures from when the GPU reaches the command (queue/scheduling latency before TOP is excluded by design — document this in the bench).

HN-7 (Lever A must not regress existing tests). After Lever A, readonly bindings get an EMPTY output Vec. AUDIT every existing test/bench that indexes outputs[i] for a readonly binding. q4km/saxpy index the WRITABLE output (q4km outputs[2]=y, saxpy the writable) — SAFE. CONFIRM no test reads back a readonly binding's bytes; if one does, update it. AT-1541 encodes this audit.

HN-8 (resident buffers reuse + debug interleaving guard). ResidentBuffers reuses allocate_device_local_buffer + the descriptor-write path from kernel_handle.rs, with a SEPARATE lifetime owned by ResidentBuffers (its own device-local buffers, command buffer, fence, query pool; query pool destroyed in Drop). The N-loop REUSES one CB + one fence + one query pool (no per-iter alloc — WARNING fix). dispatch_resident re-binds the descriptor set to resident buffers and sets resident_bound=true; dispatch_handle sets resident_bound=false. A debug_assert (NOT a session type) catches interleaving without a re-bind. Do not interleave on the same handle without a re-bind.

HN-9 (Lever A predicate centralization). All four readback loops (single-queue copy-record, single-queue memcpy, dedicated copy-record, dedicated memcpy) MUST use binding_is_readback so they agree — a binding skipped in copy-record but read in memcpy = reading uninitialized staging = corruption. Honor the M3.0 r2 'all four loops agree' note.

HN-10 (NO hardcoded coopmat shape — now ACHIEVABLE via metadata). The required shape for matmul_tile is read from metadata.coopmat (CoopMatShapeMeta), which the driver fills from the HIR-derived CoopMatShape (from the body's matrix[f16,16,16,*] types). Build CoopMatRequiredShape via coopmat_required_shape_from_meta — NOT a literal. The runtime DETECTS a coopmat kernel via metadata.coopmat.is_some(). D's @strategy tile holes vary the source dims; the metadata reflects whatever the source declares. AT-1551 (preflight drives tile selection) + AT-1552 (runtime reads shape from metadata, nothing hardcoded) prove this.

HN-11 (q4km_dequant_matmul layout — PINNED DEFINITIVELY). q (readonly_buffer[u8]) = the weight matrix as n_rows consecutive weight-rows; weight-row `row` occupies bytes [row * n_blocks_per_row * 144 .. (row+1) * n_blocks_per_row * 144], each 144-byte Q4_K_M superblock laid out exactly as M2.6 (q4km_dequant_matvec). x (readonly_buffer[f32]) = the dense input matrix, column-of-output-major: x[k * n_cols + col] is the k-th dequantized-weight-index input for output column col, k in 0..(n_blocks_per_row*256). y (buffer[f32]) = output, row-major: y[row * n_cols + col]. Each invocation i = gid(0): row = i / n_cols, col = i % n_cols; out = sum over the n_blocks_per_row superblocks of weight-row `row`, each superblock's 256 dequantized weights w[k] multiplied by x[(blk*256 + k) * n_cols + col], reusing the EXACT M2.6 inline get_scale_min_k4 + dequant. The CPU reference q4km_dequant_matmul_cpu matches this layout EXACTLY. For the 256x256 fixture: n_rows=256, n_cols=256, n_blocks_per_row=1 (one superblock per weight-row, 256 weights = 256 contraction elements). No fixture ambiguity.

HN-12 (CoopMatKey new fields — mechanical). CoopMatKey gains k + result_type. At every construction site in body.rs/coopmat.rs fill k from the contraction dim already in scope (a.n / b.m / accumulator's K) and result_type from the accumulator elem. The emitted SPIR-V must be byte-identical for matmul_tile (the key is an internal BTreeMap dedup key; OpTypeCooperativeMatrixKHR operands are M/N/use/elem, unchanged). AT-1508 asserts SPIR-V word-count identity vs the pre-M3.1 baseline.

HN-13 (metadata back-compat). load_kernel_metadata must accept schema_version 1 AND 2. A v1 sidecar (written by pre-M3.1 compiles) has no `coopmat` key; #[serde(default)] yields coopmat=None, which is dispatch-identical to a non-coopmat kernel. New compiles write schema_version=2. Do NOT reject v1 — existing on-disk sidecars and the M0..M2.6 test corpus depend on it. AT-1553 covers both directions.

## M3.1 — Cooperative-matrix dispatch + multi-row matmul + GPU-resident benchmark (r1)

### C1. Coopmat shape metadata plumbing (HIR → codegen → metadata → runtime)

The pessimistic review verified the runtime had NO way to know a kernel is coopmat or what shape it needs. r1 fixes this end-to-end:

1. **HIR** (axc-hir/src/coopmat.rs, hir.rs, lower.rs): CoopMatKey gains `k: u32` + `result_type: ScalarTy`. The existing CoopMatrixShape struct gains `result_type` + `scope: CoopMatScopeHir`. KernelAnnotations gains `coop_matrix: Option<CoopMatShape>`. During lowering, when the `cooperative_matrix` flag is set, `derive_coopmat_shape(&body)` extracts M=a.m, N=b.n, K=a.n(==b.m), a/b/c/result element types, scope=Subgroup from the (typechecked) coopmat_mul_add operands. For matmul_tile: 16×16×16, all f16, Subgroup.
2. **Codegen** (body.rs, coopmat.rs): MECHANICAL — CoopMatKey literals gain the two fields; emitted SPIR-V byte-identical (HN-12).
3. **Metadata** (metadata.rs): CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION 1→2; KernelMetadata gains `#[serde(default)] coopmat: Option<CoopMatShapeMeta>`. load_kernel_metadata accepts v1 (coopmat=None via default) and v2. Driver fills coopmat from the HIR CoopMatShape.
4. **Runtime**: builds CoopMatRequiredShape from metadata.coopmat (coopmat_required_shape_from_meta), NOT a literal. Detects coopmat via metadata.coopmat.is_some(). HN-10/AT-1551/AT-1552 are now real.

### A. Coopmat device enablement + preflight + feature pass (coopmat.rs, context.rs)

**required_device_features(binding_plan, uses_coopmat)** (CRITICAL-2/-3) derives the device-feature set from the binding plan: storage_16bit ⇐ any f16 SSBO; storage_8bit + shader_int8 ⇐ any u8/i8 SSBO; shader_int16 ⇐ q4km path; vulkan_memory_model + cooperative_matrix ⇐ uses_coopmat. See the capability→feature table.

**context.rs feature-chain assembly** (WARNING fix): all feature-struct locals at function scope, pNext assembled unconditionally for every device-SUPPORTED feature in the required superset; availability probed via Features2; an unavailable-but-needed feature is NOT force-enabled — dispatch fails closed with DeviceFeatureUnsupported. Stores coopmat_support, enabled_features, timestamp_period, compute_timestamp_valid_bits, subgroup_size.

**Preflight matcher (pure)** coopmat_shape_supported(required, support): true iff feature_present AND ∃ s∈shapes with s.m/n/k == required AND a/b/c/result component types match AND s.scope==Subgroup AND s.saturating_accumulation==false (codegen emits NONE_KHR operands — WARNING fix). query_coopmat_support uses the two-call count idiom (count==0 ⇒ empty, no second call).

**Graceful skip**: coopmat shape/scope mismatch OR subgroup_size!=32 ⇒ CoopMatUnsupported; missing storage/int feature ⇒ DeviceFeatureUnsupported. Non-coopmat f32 kernels never hit the coopmat check; f16/u8 kernels still go through the feature check.

### B. matmul_tile FIRST dispatch (dispatch_matmul_tile.rs)

Compile matmul_tile.axc (reuses M2.1 codegen). binding_plan: tile_offset (push u32), a_buf/b_buf (readonly f16 SSBO), c_buf (readwrite f16 SSBO). Build the NON-SYMMETRIC transpose-distinguishing A,B f16 tiles + C0=0 (transpose_fixture_spec). workgroups=(1,1,1). AT-1509 first asserts pipeline CREATION succeeds (proves HN-1 + 16-bit-storage feature wired). Then dispatch via dispatch_handle; read back c_buf (writable, ReadOnly a/b skipped by Lever A); compare to matmul_tile_16x16x16_f16_cpu within f16 tol. AT-1512 asserts the four transpose-variant references differ beyond tol (CRITICAL-4). On Lavapipe / subgroup!=32: typed skip. PRIMARY ACCEPTANCE (AT-1510).

### B2. Multi-row q4km_dequant_matmul (plain, dispatchable everywhere)

Layout PINNED in HN-11. 256×256 fixture (n_rows=256, n_cols=256, n_blocks_per_row=1). AT-1522 asserts pipeline creation (8-bit storage + Int8/Int16 features wired). Bit-exact within 1e-3 rel tol vs q4km_dequant_matmul_cpu (AT-1520, NOT #[ignore] — runs on Lavapipe AND NVIDIA). NO coopmat.

### B3. q4km coopmat bridge (staged, NVIDIA-only)

q4km_dequant_matmul_coopmat.axc consumes PRE-DEQUANTIZED f16 weight + f16 x SSBOs; coopmat_load/mul_add/store a 16×16 tile. Bit-close on NVIDIA; #[ignore]+preflight-skip elsewhere (AT-1521). Proves coopmat on a Q4_K_M-derived workload without shared[T,N].

### C. GPU-resident benchmark (resident.rs)

upload_resident: device-local buffers, stage-upload inputs ONCE, write descriptor set to resident buffers, allocate ONE reusable CB+fence+query pool. dispatch_resident: record cmd_reset_query_pool, write_timestamp(TOP), bind+push+dispatch, write_timestamp(BOTTOM); submit; wait; kernel_ns = masked_timestamp_delta(...) * timestamp_period; NO upload/readback in the steady-state loop; CpuFenceWall fallback when timestamps invalid. Single-allocation reuse across the N-loop. The §3.1.12-rescoped metric: upload once, dispatch N, measure kernel time.

### D. Per-vendor @strategy tile holes

matmul_f32_tiled.axc declares @strategy { tile_m, tile_n }. Ordinary M2.3 holes (enumerator unchanged). For coopmat variants, each candidate tile is VALIDATED against ctx.coopmat_support() via coopmat_shape_supported — preflight DRIVES selection, nothing hardcoded. The f32 tiled holes affect only workgroup/loop tiling (no coopmat constraint).

### E. Lever A — skip readback of readonly bindings (kernel_handle.rs)

binding_is_readback(access, output_size) = output_size>0 && access != ReadOnly. Used in ALL FOUR readback loops (HN-9). ReadOnly bindings never device→staging copied, never HOST barrier'd, never invalidated, empty output Vec. WriteOnly/ReadWrite byte-exact. Re-lands M3.0 Lever A WITHOUT the reverted ReBAR Lever B.

design_md_additions:
## 3.1.13 M3.1 — Cooperative-matrix dispatch + multi-row matmul + GPU-resident benchmark

M3.1 makes the M2.1 cooperative-matrix codegen EXECUTE on real tensor cores for the first time, adds a multi-row Q4_K_M matmul, and builds the GPU-resident benchmark methodology that M3.0's `<1 ms` gate was re-scoped onto (§3.1.12 r2). The emitted coopmat SPIR-V is UNCHANGED from M2.1; M3.1 is a RUNTIME + metadata + kernel + benchmark milestone. The only codegen touch is a mechanical internal-cache-key extension (CoopMatKey gains K + result_type) that leaves the emitted module byte-identical.

### Coopmat shape metadata (HIR → sidecar → runtime)

Previously the runtime had no way to know a kernel used cooperative matrices or what shape it required: `@cooperative_matrix` was a bare bool, `CoopMatKey` carried no K and no result type, and the metadata sidecar carried nothing coopmat. M3.1 plumbs the shape end-to-end. The HIR derives a kernel-level `CoopMatShape{m,n,k,a/b/c/result element types, scope}` from the body's `matrix[T,M,N,use]` types of the coopmat ops (reusing the M2.1 type-check guarantees, so K = a.n = b.m). The metadata sidecar gains a `coopmat: Option<CoopMatShapeMeta>` field; `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is bumped 1→2 and `load_kernel_metadata` accepts both versions (a v1 sidecar with no field deserializes to `None` via `#[serde(default)]`, which is dispatch-identical to a non-coopmat kernel). The runtime builds the required shape FROM the metadata — nothing is hardcoded.

### Device-feature enablement: the capability→feature pass

spirv-val validates a module but does NOT check that the device features its capabilities require are enabled — passing spirv-val does NOT imply `vkCreateComputePipelines` will succeed. M3.1 adds a binding-plan-driven `required_device_features` pass mapping each EMITTED SPIR-V capability to the Vulkan device feature the runtime must enable:

| SPIR-V capability | trigger | Vulkan device feature |
|---|---|---|
| VulkanMemoryModel | coopmat op used | VkPhysicalDeviceVulkanMemoryModelFeatures.vulkanMemoryModel (+DeviceScope) |
| CooperativeMatrixKHR | coopmat op used | VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix ext + VkPhysicalDeviceCooperativeMatrixFeaturesKHR.cooperativeMatrix |
| StorageBuffer16BitAccess | any f16 SSBO | VkPhysicalDevice16BitStorageFeatures.storageBuffer16BitAccess |
| StorageBuffer8BitAccess | any u8/i8 SSBO | VkPhysicalDevice8BitStorageFeatures.storageBuffer8BitAccess |
| Int8 | u8/i8 SSBO / ptr_read_u8 | VkPhysicalDeviceShaderFloat16Int8Features.shaderInt8 |
| Int16 | f16_bits_to_f32 | VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures.shaderInt16 |

Matmul_tile is the FIRST f16-SSBO kernel ever dispatched (it needs `storageBuffer16BitAccess` on top of the memory-model + coopmat features); the multi-row q4km kernel is the first 8-bit-storage + Int8/Int16 dispatch. The runtime enables the device-SUPPORTED subset of this superset at context creation (all feature-struct locals at function scope so they outlive `create_device`, chain assembled unconditionally), and a kernel that needs a feature the device lacks FAILS CLOSED with the typed `DeviceFeatureUnsupported` skip — never enable-and-hope.

### Preflight, subgroup guard, graceful skip

A preflight queries `vkGetPhysicalDeviceCooperativeMatrixPropertiesKHR` for the device's supported `(M,N,K,AType,BType,CType,ResultType,scope,saturatingAccumulation)` tuples and the `cooperativeMatrix` feature. A pure matcher checks the metadata-derived required shape (16×16×16 f16, Subgroup, non-saturating) against that set. Because matmul_tile is `@workgroup(32,1,1)` and assumes one 32-lane subgroup == one tile, the dispatch path additionally REQUIRES `subgroupSize == 32`; a wave64/SIMD16 device that advertises the shape is SKIPPED (not miscomputed). When unsupported — Lavapipe, software, wrong subgroup size, or the `force_no_coopmat` CI option — the dispatch returns `DispatchError::CoopMatUnsupported` and tests/benches SKIP cleanly. The same single `matmul_tile.axc` SKIPS on Lavapipe and DISPATCHES on NVIDIA Blackwell — the preflight, not the source, decides. The NVIDIA runner is a MANDATORY sign-off gate: an all-device skip of the first-dispatch proof is a milestone FAIL.

### Multi-row Q4_K_M matmul (real workload) — staged honestly

`q4km_dequant_matmul.axc` extends M2.6's single-row matvec to an N-row × M-col output, each invocation computing one output via the proven Q4_K_M dequant dot-product, bit-exact vs a CPU reference for a 256×256 fixture, on Lavapipe AND NVIDIA (a regular, non-ignored GPU test). The TRUE single-kernel `dequant → shared-f16-tile → coopmat` fusion needs `shared[T,N]` (FG.6, deferred to M3.2), so M3.1 delivers two honest pieces: the plain multi-row matmul (the bit-exact deliverable, runs everywhere) plus a pre-dequantized-input coopmat bridge (`q4km_dequant_matmul_coopmat.axc`, NVIDIA-only proof that coopmat runs on a Q4_K_M-derived workload).

### GPU-resident benchmark methodology

The thesis-relevant metric is **upload weights ONCE to resident VRAM, dispatch N times, measure KERNEL time** — exactly how llama.cpp inference works. M3.1 adds `upload_resident` / `dispatch_resident` / `readback_resident`: inputs are staged once, the descriptor set bound to resident device-local buffers, and each iteration records ONLY the compute submit, timed by `vkCmdWriteTimestamp` × 2 (`elapsed = (end−begin) · timestampPeriod`, each endpoint masked to `timestampValidBits` before subtraction), with a CPU fence-wall fallback recorded in `ResidentDispatchTiming.timing_source`. The N-loop reuses one command buffer, fence, and query pool. The 4096×4096 f32 resident matmul reports **effective TFLOPS** (the honest, reproducible in-tree number); the `≥50%-of-cuBLAS` comparison is an external estimate, labeled as such (the project is CUDA-free by thesis) — only effective TFLOPS is asserted.

### Per-vendor @strategy tile holes and Lever A re-land

Tile dimensions are ordinary M2.3 `@strategy` holes; for coopmat variants each candidate is VALIDATED against the preflight supported set (preflight DRIVES selection). Lever A is re-landed cleanly (without the reverted ReBAR Lever B): a binding is read back iff `output_size > 0 && access != ReadOnly`, applied uniformly across all four readback loops; read-only inputs skip the device→staging copy, the HOST_READ barrier, and the invalidate.
